messages.subject: Per-session object assignment
parts:
Hi,
I am not sure if I understanding this correctly, but it seems that <<- assignment is for global variable that could be shared among different clients right?

I have the following code:

server <- function(input,output,session){
  flagStem = TRUE

model <- reactive({
    modelRes<-NA
    input$retrain
      withProgress({     
        if(isolate({input$stem}) == flagStem)
             flag = FALSE
        else flag=TRUE
        print(paste("Before:",isolate({input$stem}),",",flagStem,",",flag,sep=""))
        .....
        flagStem <<- isolate({input$stem})
        print(paste("After:",isolate({input$stem}),",",flagStem,sep=""))
        ...
      })
    
    return(modelRes)
  })


Here I defined a flagStem boolean var, to store the previous status of a checkboxInput "stem" within the same session.
If the checkbox is unchanged, flag = FALSE. And input$retrain is an action button.

The problem here is that if I use  flagStem <- isolate({input$stem}) instead of  <<- ,
every time when I click the input$retrain button, the flag$stem remains "TRUE", while within the model reactive(), it is changed to FALSE. 
So I am a little bit confused here. Appreciate your help!

Yinghao

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Per-session object assignment
parts:
<<- won't set it for all clients, because the place the variable is declared (flagStem = TRUE) is inside the server function. The <<- operator doesn't automatically assign to the global environment; instead, it will look up the chain of lexical parent environments until it finds a matching variable name, and only if it never finds one does it assign to the global environment.

That being said, I suspect this code can be factored much more "reactively"--alarm bells should go off in your head if you try to assign to outer-scoped variables from within a reactive. Can you say a little more about what you're trying to do here?

Hi Joe, thank you for your reply. 
What I am doing here is that I have created a checkbox for word stemming. Once I click the input$retrain action button, a model will be trained with/without stemming by calling a topicModel() function. In this function, a term-document matrix is generated and saved.  
The logic here is, if user click the train button the second time without changing the stemming checkbox,  the topic model function will skip the matrix generation part and directly use the one that has already been saved.
As a result, I want to track the previous value and current value of the checkbox for the user, if they click the retrain button.

Yinghao

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Per-session object assignment
parts:
I think it should be like this.

termDocMatrix <- reactive({
  # calculate something, using input$stem in the process--don't use isolate()
})

model <- eventReactive(input$retrain, {
  # use termDocMatrix() and topicModel() to create and return the model
}, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

Then elsewhere in your app you can refer to model().

See http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/action-buttons.html for details on eventReactive, but basically it creates a reactive expression that only invalidates when input$retrain is clicked.

The general idea is that if you want something to be recalculated on a different schedule than something else (in this case, the model and the term document matrix) then they should be in separate reactives. This is the main purpose of reactives: to let derived values be calculated the minimal amount while still maintaining correctness.
